stormAlert.headline: Get to shore now!
stormAlert.body: A level 2 storm warning is in effect near {{spotName}} — staying on the water with a SUP is forbidden and life-threatening.

steps.1: Paddle to the nearest shore — not necessarily back to your starting point if that is farther away.
steps.2: If you cannot reach the shore: kneel down, reduce your wind profile, keep your ankle leash on.
steps.3: If you are in trouble, call water rescue: +36 30 383 8383.

water.level: River level at the assigned gauge (source: vizugy.hu / OVF).

floodAlert.headline: Get ashore immediately!
floodAlert.body: A level III flood alert is in effect near {{spotName}} — being on the flooded river with a SUP is forbidden and life-threatening.

steps.1: Paddle to the nearest safe bank right away — you will not be able to paddle back against a flooding river.
steps.2: Stay clear of overhanging trees, bridges and floating debris: the current pushes you into them and the board can flip underneath.
steps.3: If you are in trouble, call water rescue: +36 30 383 8383.

list.title: Basic info
list.lead: What's allowed, what isn't, and what to watch for — navigation rules, safety notes and practical info for the ten most popular Hungarian SUP waters. This isn't playful trivia — it's what you need to know before you get on the water.

detail.lastVerified: Last verified: 2026-09-26. Rules change from time to time — if in doubt, check the sources listed below or the current notice from the local authority or operator.
detail.relatedLeash: Leash — what it's for and which type you need
detail.relatedPfd: Life vest — when you can't skip it

level1.signal: about 45 flashes/minute · gusts of 40–60 km/h expected, signals at least 30 minutes before the wind arrives
level1.action: swimmers: within 500 m of the shore · on Lake Balaton on a SUP: within 100 m

level2.action: launching and staying on the water is strictly forbidden

legalBasis.0: Act XLII of 2000, Section 87, point 44 — definition of “water sports equipment” (Water Transport Act)
legalBasis.2: Decree 46/2001 (XII. 27.) BM — basic rules for being on open water
legalBasis.3: Decree 17/2002 (III. 7.) KöViM — the register of designated waterways (this determines which waters the Navigation Regulations apply to)

balaton.title: Lake Balaton
balaton.tag: Classified as bathing equipment · storm warning system active

rules.0: Lake Balaton is a waterway, so the Navigation Rules apply here: by law a SUP is “water sports equipment” (a buoyant, steerable craft that is neither a ship nor a boat) — not bathing equipment.
rules.1: Paddlers aged 14+ who can swim must wear at least a buoyancy aid OR a safety ankle leash (Navigation Rules Part II, Article 4.05, point 3). The only exception is learning: at a bathing site, right next to the shore, without disturbing swimmers, with a person able to help.
rules.2: Distance from shore on a SUP, on both shores: normally up to 500 m; at a level I storm warning — and, while the warning service is paused, in wind of Beaufort 4–6 — up to 100 m; at a level II warning, or while the service is paused in wind above Beaufort 6, being on the water is prohibited (Navigation Rules Part II, Article 9.12, point 4a).
rules.3: Launching is forbidden in shipping lanes, near harbours and docks, near navigation buoys, in designated windsurfing, kayaking and wakeboarding zones, near bridges (e.g. the Tihany strait), anywhere marked with a prohibition sign, and in protected nature areas.
rules.4: Wearing a life vest is always mandatory for anyone under 14 and for non-swimmers.

balaton.safetyIntro: Lake Balaton's storm warning system runs from April to October — flashing yellow signals at fixed shore stations and on mobile beach lamps.

safetyNotes.0: Lake Balaton is known for storms that form very quickly — this is the single most important safety message for this lake.
safetyNotes.1: Water rescue hotline: 1817, general emergency number: 112.

practical.0: The storm warning system only operates between April 1 and October 31 — outside that window there is no light-signal warning at all, so pay extra attention on your own.
practical.1: Check out our Lake Balaton spots for current wind and water data.

velencei-to.title: Lake Velence
velencei-to.tag: Classified as bathing equipment · storm warning system in operation

rules.0: Lake Velence is a waterway, so the Navigation Rules apply: a SUP is “water sports equipment”. Paddlers aged 14+ who can swim need at least a buoyancy aid OR a safety ankle leash; under-14s and non-swimmers need a life jacket (Part II, Article 4.05, point 3).
rules.1: Operating small craft and boats with internal combustion engines is prohibited across the ENTIRE lake — this is what makes Lake Velence a quiet water.
rules.2: The Lake Velence chapter of the Navigation Rules (Article 9.21) sets no distance-from-shore limit for SUPs — only for boats and sailing sports equipment. The widely quoted “500 metre rule” is the level I storm warning limit for swimmers and boats; it is sensible to keep to it on a SUP too (see below).
rules.3: Swimming is prohibited in the fairway, within 100 m of the buoys marking it, in and within 100 m of harbours and water sports courses, and wherever a sign forbids it — avoid these places on a SUP too.
rules.4: No water sports course may be designated within 150 metres of a designated bathing area — the strip in front of the beaches belongs to swimmers.
rules.5: Most of the lake is reed bed; open water is reached through channels and entrances. It is easy to get lost in the reeds, and you cannot land just anywhere.

velencei-to.safetyIntro: From 1 April to 31 October, Lake Velence is covered by the same storm forecasting and storm warning service as Lake Balaton and Lake Tisza.

safetyNotes.0: A shallow lake that warms quickly — and that the wind whips up just as quickly. Shallow water produces short, steep waves, which are harder to handle on a SUP than long swell.
safetyNotes.1: Water rescue emergency line: 1817, general emergency number: 112.

practical.0: Launch from the beaches at Agárd and Velence.
practical.1: See our Lake Velence spots with current wind and water data.

tisza-to.title: Lake Tisza
tisza-to.tag: Kisköre reservoir · classified as water sports equipment

rules.0: Here a SUP is legally classified as "water sports equipment" — unlike Lake Balaton and Lake Velence. For a swimmer aged 14 or over doing normal paddling, wearing a life vest OR a safety ankle leash is enough; the local operator (SUP Bázis) cites this directly, with a precise legal reference.
rules.1: Wearing a life vest is always mandatory for anyone under 14, for non-swimmers, and for everyone while fishing or using a boat hook.
rules.2: The bathing decree lets swimmers go up to 500 m from the shore of Lake Tisza without an escort. The Navigation Rules set no separate distance for SUPs — keeping within 500 m is still sensible.
rules.3: Motor-restricted nature reserve zones — Porong-tava, Ispán-tava, Hód, Gaznyilas, Partos-fenék, Óhalászi-holtág — allow paddling/SUP and electric motors but not combustion engines: these are, somewhat counterintuitively, the quieter, calmer stretches for paddlers, not no-go zones.
rules.4: Southwest of route 33, combustion engines are capped at 4 kW.
rules.5: Right of way on the water: large vessels first, then sailboats, then paddlers/SUP, and only then motorboats — motorised rental boats must give way to paddlers.

tisza-to.safetyIntro: The same storm warning system operates here as on Lake Balaton.

safetyNotes.0: The table below uses the same level logic as Lake Balaton.
safetyNotes.1: If you're unsure about local wind conditions, ask the shore operators — they know the day-to-day situation best.

practical.0: Main launch points: Poroszló (Albatrosz Harbour) and Tiszafüred.
practical.1: Local rental/instruction operators (e.g. SUP Bázis in Poroszló) can give you a fresh, local briefing before you launch.

ferto-to.title: Lake Fertő

rules.0: Lake Fertő is a waterway and also part of Fertő–Hanság National Park. According to the national park, nearly 90% of the Hungarian side is reed marsh, broken only by the inner lakes and a network of channels; the whole area is protected, and parts of it strictly protected.
rules.1: You may paddle individually with your own gear — EXCEPT in strictly protected areas marked by signs. According to the national park, the open water on the Hungarian side can be reached from Fertőrákos Bay (North Harbour), from the Virágosmajor harbour and channel, and from the Sopron Channel. Which inner lakes and channels are open at any given time is set by the signs on site — always follow them.
rules.2: Operating small craft and boats with internal combustion engines is prohibited across the entire lake.
rules.3: The Sopron channels and the loop channels connected to them are navigable; launch from there or from the lake's harbours (Virágosmajor, Fertőrákos).

ferto-to.safetyIntro: From 1 April to 31 October a storm forecasting and storm warning service operates on Lake Fertő — the levels are the same as on Lake Balaton.

safetyNotes.0: The reed channels are only 2–3 metres wide with reed on both sides: it is easy to get lost, and you cannot climb out just anywhere. Take a map, and tell someone where you are heading.
safetyNotes.1: Lake Fertő averages barely a metre in depth and is highly exposed to wind — the wind whips it up fast, and the reed bed is not a landing place.

practical.0: On the Hungarian side, launch at Fertőrákos and Virágosmajor.
practical.1: For an organised event with several participants, contact the Fertő–Hanság National Park Directorate — this is protected land.
practical.2: See our Fertőrákos spot with current wind and storm warning data.

duna.title: Danube
duna.tag: Budapest stretch · classified as water sports equipment

rules.0: Here a SUP is legally classified as "water sports equipment" — wearing a life vest or safety ankle leash is mandatory, and the water police enforce it.
rules.1: Staying inside the marked shipping lane (between red and green buoys) is forbidden; if you need to cross it, do so as quickly as possible.
rules.2: A 100 m exclusion zone applies around navigation buoys, large vessels and floating work equipment.
rules.3: A 300 m exclusion zone applies around locks and hydraulic structures; 100 m around bridges, water intakes and ferry crossings.
rules.4: Night paddling is forbidden; so is staying in ports, mooring areas, and designated water-ski/jet-ski lanes.
rules.5: Group or organised SUP events need prior coordination with the navigation authority — a formal navigation closure has already been issued for one such event on the Budapest stretch.
rules.6: During icy periods the authority can impose a full navigation ban on small craft and water sports equipment — always check current notices in winter.

safetyNotes.0: Expect commercial ship traffic and wake, strong eddies and suction near hydraulic structures, hypothermia risk, and drowning risk at night or in poor visibility.
safetyNotes.1: The Danube's current can be significant even on stretches that look calm — if you're unsure, stay close to shore and avoid the main channel.

practical.0: Known Budapest launch points: Római-part (Béke boathouse), Csepel (Kolonics György Water Sports Centre), the Ráckeve branch of the Danube (BEAC), the Pesterzsébet SUP base, and local rental operators around Szentendre and Göd.
practical.1: Check out our Budapest spots for current water conditions.

rsd.title: Ráckeve (Soroksár) Danube Arm
rsd.tag: Waterway · water sports equipment · engine restrictions

rules.0: The whole arm (river km 58–0) is a designated waterway, so the same rule applies as on the Danube: a SUP is “water sports equipment”, and wearing a life vest or a safety ankle leash is mandatory. Under-14s and non-swimmers need a life vest.
rules.1: COMPLETELY CLOSED AREA: at Rózsa Island, in the western side branch of the arm (Büdös-sarok), a protected zone is marked with signs and buoys where travel by any watercraft is prohibited.
rules.2: At the Kvassay lock it is prohibited to enter the power plant branch by boat or to moor there.
rules.3: Operating small craft and boats with internal combustion engines is restricted for environmental reasons, and between 21:00 and 06:00 it is prohibited along the entire arm — which makes this the quietest Danube water near the capital.
rules.4: Between river km 24.5 and 32.5, combustion engines are entirely prohibited in the right-side branches (per the decree, along the Opera, Sóskás, Ráfás and Csupi islands); in the main channel over the same stretch the limit is 5 km/h, without creating waves or suction. The same 5 km/h applies at the Dömsöd ferry, between river km 10 and 11.5.
rules.5: Between river km 35 and 43 there are prohibited and speed-restricted stretches protecting floating bogs (the Dunavarsány floating bog, the Taksony backwater, and the right-bank strip between Taksony Vezér Bridge and Taksony Island) — avoid the bogs on a paddleboard too.
rules.6: Keep clear of locks and hydraulic structures by 300 metres, and of bridges, ferry crossings and water intakes by 100 metres. The arm is closed at both ends by the Kvassay and Tass locks.

safetyNotes.0: The arm behaves like still water with minimal current, which makes it beginner friendly. On the long straight stretches, though, the wind carries a board away just as it would on a lake, and paddling back into the wind is much harder.
safetyNotes.1: In summer there is heavy motorboat traffic on the unrestricted stretches; expect wake, and boats pulling out suddenly from jetties.

practical.0: Known launch points: Ráckeve, Szigetszentmiklós, Dunavarsány, Tass, and on the Budapest side the Soroksár stretch.
practical.1: The side branches closed to combustion engines (Opera, Sóskás, Ráfás and Csupi islands) are the quietest and best SUP water on the whole arm.
practical.2: The navigation restrictions and the lock operating schedule are published by the Central Danube Valley Water Directorate — worth a look before a longer tour.

tisza.title: Tisza river
tisza.tag: River · water level is the main safety factor

rules.0: The main Hungarian stretches of the Tisza are waterways (Decree 17/2002 KöViM), so the Navigation Rules apply: a SUP is “water sports equipment”. Paddlers aged 14+ who can swim need at least a buoyancy aid OR a safety ankle leash; under-14s and non-swimmers need a life jacket (Part II, Article 4.05, point 3). On moving water, use a quick-release leash attached at the waist.
rules.1: On some river sections, commercial tour operators ask for a registration form before you set off — that's operator policy, not a legal requirement.

safetyNotes.0: Water level is the main danger here: at low water, exposed rocks and gravel bars are a hazard; at high water, the current runs well above normal and low banks can become impossible to land on safely. Always check the current water level before you go.
safetyNotes.1: Never attempt to cross a weir or dam without using the marked lock or bypass channel — doing so can be fatal. Only the marked lock/channel is safe for kayaks, canoes and SUPs (e.g. at the Kisköre and Tiszalök dams).
safetyNotes.2: On the upper Tisza, near Visó, there's also a submerged-rock hazard — this mostly matters for multi-day kayak/canoe tours rather than local SUP paddling.
safetyNotes.3: If you're unsure about the water level, ask local tour operators or check the live water level forecast (see below).

practical.0: A popular section for beginners and intermediates: Tiszabecs → Szatmárcseke on the upper river — a comfortable pace is around 15–25 km/day.
practical.1: Live water level forecast: eveznijo.hu's "Vízállás előrejelzés" — check it before you go.
practical.2: Backwaters — the oxbow lakes along the river — offer calmer, more predictable water than the Tisza's main channel, a good choice for beginners or a calmer day.

rules.0: The whole length of the Hármas-Körös (river km 91–0) is a designated waterway, so a SUP counts as “water sports equipment” here too: a swimmer over 14 needs a life vest or a safety ankle leash, while under-14s and non-swimmers need a life vest.
rules.1: The floodplain belongs to Körös–Maros National Park. Combustion-engine boats may only travel on the river itself — they are prohibited on the backwaters and borrow pits inside the floodplain. That is no restriction for paddlers; it is exactly what makes the backwaters the quietest water here.
rules.2: Choose your speed so that the waves and noise you create are as small as possible.
rules.3: In a protected natural area you may not leave waste behind, and fires may only be lit at designated fire sites.
rules.4: Paddling downstream from Gyomaendrőd, the Békésszentandrás weir closes the river. The ONLY way through is the navigation lock, for touring canoes and kayaks, according to the water directorate, single boats between 08:00–09:00 and 16:00–18:00, and groups continuously 08:00–18:00 from 1 March to 30 November — water conditions permitting. Call the lock before setting out (+36 30 743 3729).

safetyNotes.0: NEVER try to pass over a weir or spillway — it can be fatal. At the Békésszentandrás weir the navigation lock is the only viable route, and it has to be arranged in advance.
safetyNotes.1: Water level is the main safety factor here too: shoals and fords at low water, much stronger current at high water, and steep banks that can become impossible to land on.
safetyNotes.2: Most of the floodplain banks are protected natural areas — land at the designated stops, not wherever you happen to be able to.

practical.0: Launch at Gyomaendrőd: the Csicsegő water tour stop at the road bridge towards Dévaványa/Körösladány, on the left bank.
practical.1: The floodplain backwaters — former meanders cut off during the 19th-century river regulation — give calmer, more predictable water than the main channel. The same logic as on the Tisza.
practical.2: The Kettős-Körös (river km 23–0) and the lower Sebes-Körös (river km 10–0) are designated waterways too, under the same rules.

szigetkoz.title: Szigetköz
szigetkoz.tag: Mosoni-Duna and side branches · permit and notification required

rules.0: The Mosoni-Duna is a designated waterway (river km 14–0), so a SUP is “water sports equipment”: a swimmer over 14 needs a life vest or a safety ankle leash, while under-14s and non-swimmers need a life vest.
rules.1: MOST IMPORTANT: every water body in the Szigetköz lies within a protected area, so travelling on them by any craft REQUIRES A PERMIT AND NOTIFICATION. Sort this out before you set off, not on the water.
rules.2: The side branch system is navigable with human-powered craft (kayak, canoe, SUP); Szigetköz rules place strict limits on combustion engines.
rules.3: The side branch system has many sills and weirs: on a longer tour expect 8–10 portages.
rules.4: In a protected natural area you may not leave waste behind, and fires may only be lit at designated places.

safetyNotes.0: The branch system is intricate and its flow depends on hydraulic structures: the same branch can be paddleable one day and impassable the next. Without solid local knowledge, take a guide or join an organised tour.
safetyNotes.1: Bring closed water shoes or sandals for the portages — bare feet on the rocks invite injury.
safetyNotes.2: Carry your phone in a waterproof case along with a local contact number and a map: there is no mobile coverage everywhere in the side branches.

practical.0: Arrange the permit and notification before departure — through the Hello Szigetköz permit page.
practical.1: The main Mosoni-Duna channel is continuously paddleable down to Győr and involves the fewest portages — that is the beginner's entry point.
practical.2: See our Győr spot with current wind and water data.

orfu.title: Orfű lakes
orfu.tag: Not a designated waterway · Lake Pécs is the SUP water

rules.0: The Orfű lakes are NOT on the register of designated waterways, so the Navigation Regulations are not the starting point here. What governs instead are the bathing rules and the local regime: the Orfű municipality's rules, the operator, and the angling association.
rules.1: The SUP water is Lake Pécs (69 hectares, a valley-dam reservoir). Anyone can launch from the large floating jetty of the Active Water Tourism Centre — about 200 metres from the village centre, on the south-eastern shore — where the water is waist deep, good for beginners too.
rules.2: On Lake Orfű the angling rules state that placing any kind of watercraft on the lake is prohibited — do not take your board there.
rules.3: Approaching the dam by any watercraft within 50 metres is prohibited; a line of buoys marks the limit.
rules.4: A life vest is not legally required here, but in the middle of the lake you are just as alone as anywhere else — always wear your leash.

safetyNotes.0: This is a valley-dam reservoir: the bottom can drop away steeply near the shore, and the area around the dam is the most dangerous point — take the buoy line seriously.
safetyNotes.1: In the Mecsek hills the wind follows the valley and picks up suddenly before a thunderstorm. From the middle of the lake the shore is 10–15 minutes of paddling — reckon with that if the weather turns.

practical.0: Several local operators rent gear on Lake Pécs (SUP, kayak, canoe, pedalo) — the simplest way in for a beginner.
practical.1: The Orfű municipality's rules govern the resort area: park only in the designated area, and do not drive down to the shore.
practical.2: Both Lake Pécs and Lake Orfű are officially considered suitable for bathing — but take a watercraft onto Lake Pécs only.

sources.title: Sources
sources.hint: What we say about the rules on this page comes from these sources. Rules can change: check the source and the signs on site before you set out — if they differ, they take precedence. We also check the sources automatically every quarter.
